episodes.title: Hydra of Lerna
episodes.hotspot: Field heat and energy contribute 44.5% of the baseline footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: A 3.2 t, nine-headed Hydra reconstructed as a hazardous field-control event: cutting is only the first step, while cauterisation, logistics and containment create a 1.35 t CO₂e footprint.
episodes.functionalUnit: One Hydra neutralisation and containment event, modelled as one field response cycle from arrival to the immortal head sealed under the boulder and the containment pit closed.

evidence.basis: The canonical nine-headed Hydra and its regeneration problem define the intervention logic. The approved episode uses an 11 m, 3.2 t semi-aquatic reconstruction and models neutralisation as cutting, thermal cauterisation and controlled containment with modern field-response flows and emission-factor proxies.
evidence.uncertainty: Body mass scales fuel, lime, sheeting and freight and moves the result from 1.01 to 1.88 t CO₂e; the quicklime emission factor is a secondary proxy sensitivity that does not change the hotspot story.

episodes.title: The Garden of the Hesperides
episodes.hotspot: The 10 µm gold gilding layer contributes 296.4 kg CO₂e, or 88.2% of the modeled total.
episodes.featuredDescription: Three golden apples reconstructed as one annual guarded orchard service: a 10 µm gold skin is enough to make primary gold dominate the 336 kg CO₂e baseline while water, electricity and freight remain minor.
episodes.functionalUnit: One annual guarded presentation of three golden apples from the Hesperidean orchard gate.

evidence.basis: The documented myth constrains the guarded golden fruit and Ladon. The approved episode reconstructs three 80 mm apples, a 10 µm gold surface and one year of western Mediterranean orchard support using literature benchmarks, engineering assumptions, DEFRA 2026 factors and a separately disclosed primary-gold proxy.
evidence.uncertainty: Gold thickness and gold-source intensity dominate interpretation: the physical sensitivity spans 188–781 kg CO₂e and the gold-factor sensitivity spans 139–484 kg CO₂e.

episodes.title: Santa's Sleigh
episodes.hotspot: Reindeer forage contributes 177.7 kg CO₂e, or 67% of the baseline footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: A reusable 4.2 m sleigh reconstructed as a one-night delivery system: 267 kg CO₂e per Christmas Eve mission, with reindeer forage dominating the baseline and feeding-rate and harness assumptions controlling the main sensitivities.
episodes.functionalUnit: One reusable airborne gift-delivery sleigh completing one Christmas Eve mission.

evidence.basis: The approved episode uses a canonical eight-reindeer motive team and reconstructs one 4.2 m reusable sleigh with a 160 kg laminated-wood body, 40 kg steel runners and brackets, a 30 kg leather/textile harness and a twelve-mission lifetime. DEFRA 2026 is prioritized for physical material, forage and logistics flows, with declared modern proxies where no dedicated factor exists.
evidence.uncertainty: Feeding rate moves the total from 208 to 326 kg CO₂e, while changing the harness factor moves it from 211 to 351 kg CO₂e. Magic flight energy remains excluded rather than receiving an invented emission factor.

episodes.title: Baba Yaga's Hut
episodes.hotspot: Metal hardware and leg bracing contribute 1.72 t CO₂e, or 46.1% of the baseline footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: A 5.87 t Slavic walking forest hut reconstructed from logs, metal bracing, chimney, glazing and commissioning flows: the 3.73 t CO₂e baseline is driven by the structure that lets the cabin stand on legs, not by magic.
episodes.functionalUnit: One reconstructed walking hut, delivered and commissioned once (reference flow: one cabin; 30-year service context).

evidence.basis: Slavic folklore supplies the walking-hut form while the approved episode supplies an explicit engineering reconstruction: a 3.6 × 3.0 m log-cabin envelope, 5.87 t modeled mass, two structural bird-leg supports, workshop electricity, freight and installation. DEFRA 2026 is prioritized for the disclosed physical flows and modern proxies are declared where exact factors do not exist.
evidence.uncertainty: Physical scaling is the largest uncertainty: the mass sensitivity moves the result from 2.77 to 5.55 t CO₂e. Material origin is also consequential, shifting the modeled footprint from 1.62 t CO₂e with reused timber and recycled metal to 4.20 t CO₂e in the high-material-intensity case.

episodes.title: Sisyphus
episodes.featuredDescription: A finite slice of an eternal punishment: one reusable 5.0 t limestone boulder, a 500 m slope, 1,000 ascent-return cycles and a material loop that closes while the energy loop does not.
episodes.functionalUnit: Construction and execution of 1,000 complete punishment cycles using one reusable 5.0 t limestone boulder on a 500 m slope with 100 m vertical rise.

evidence.basis: The Homeric punishment loop defines the repeated function. Boulder geometry, slope mechanics and conversion efficiency are explicit reconstructions; DEFRA 2026 aggregate and electricity-equivalent factors provide the physical accounting proxies.
evidence.uncertainty: The finite cycle count, 20% conversion efficiency and electricity-equivalent energy proxy control interpretation of an otherwise unbounded punishment.

episodes.title: Talos
episodes.featuredDescription: A 25 m bronze guardian reconstructed as a mobility system: manufacture is significant, but three daily circuits of Crete make patrol energy the overwhelming life-cycle hotspot.
episodes.functionalUnit: Manufacture and 30 years of operation of one 25 m bronze Talos providing continuous coastal defence for Crete: three 1,046 km patrol circuits per day, one 2 t boulder throw per circuit and one red-heat deterrence event per month.

evidence.basis: Apollonius Rhodius and Pseudo-Apollodorus define the guardian behaviours. Height, shell thickness, coastline route, locomotion energy and service life are explicit engineering assumptions; modern DEFRA factors are used as proxies.
evidence.uncertainty: The patrol-energy proxy, assumed 1,046 km circuit and 30-year duty cycle dominate the model because operation overwhelms manufacture.

episodes.title: Mjölnir
episodes.hotspot: Lightning-equivalent discharge contributes 99.43% of the footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: A reusable 46.7 kg iron hammer becomes an energy system once a 1 GJ thunder-equivalent event is repeated over 1,000 combat cycles: discharge energy overwhelms manufacture and flight.
episodes.functionalUnit: Manufacture and deployment of one reusable Mjölnir-class iron hammer over 1,000 combat cycles, each with a 50 m outbound flight, a 50 m powered return and one 1 GJ lightning-equivalent discharge.

evidence.basis: Skáldskaparmál §43 defines the iron head, short haft, return behaviour and durability. Dimensions, flight speed, return efficiency and the thunder-equivalent discharge are explicit modelling assumptions.
evidence.uncertainty: The 1 GJ discharge scenario is not specified by the cited literary passage and contributes almost the entire headline footprint.

episodes.title: The Minotaur's Labyrinth
episodes.hotspot: Worked stone contributes 75.1% of lifecycle GWP; initial construction is 92.4%.
episodes.featuredDescription: A Knossos-scale two-level maze reconstructed as a navigation-denial system: 18.595 kt CO₂e over 30 years, while a 24 kg thread defeats the material system by preserving the way back.
episodes.functionalUnit: Construction and 30 years of material maintenance for one two-level, Knossos-scale Labyrinth with a 22,000 m² plan footprint, designed to confine one Minotaur and defeat unaided navigation; Ariadne's thread is quantified separately.

evidence.basis: Pseudo-Apollodorus and Diodorus define the navigation-denial function. The Palace of Knossos provides the 22,000 m² scale benchmark; levels, routes, wall geometry and material quantities are reconstructed.
evidence.uncertainty: Maze geometry, passage-network length and worked-stone quantities are the principal reconstruction choices behind the materials-dominated result.

episodes.title: Atlantis
episodes.hotspot: Initial construction contributes 58.4% of lifecycle GWP; water supply and treatment add 27.4%.
episodes.featuredDescription: Plato's concentric royal-harbor core reconstructed as a 100-year urban system: 8.41 km² of buildable land, 7.57 Mm² GFA and 500,000 residents, with the result dominated by construction and highly sensitive to where the city boundary is drawn.
episodes.functionalUnit: Construction, material maintenance and 100 years of water supply and treatment for one concentric Atlantean royal-harbor core with 8.41 km² of buildable land, 7.57 million m² of gross floor area and 500,000 operational residents.

evidence.basis: Plato's Critias constrains the concentric urban geometry. Density, material quantities, population, service life and modern emission-factor proxies are explicit reconstruction assumptions.
evidence.uncertainty: The spatial system boundary is dominant: alternative readings move the result from 1.94 Mt to 3.62 Mt to 33.04 Mt CO₂e.

episodes.title: Trojan Horse
episodes.hotspot: Primary timber contributes 45.2%; timber + rope together account for 77.2% of the main result.
episodes.featuredDescription: A one-use hollow timber machine reconstructed around a 50-warrior payload: 25 m³ of finished timber, 16.52 t rolling mass and a footprint driven far more by materials than by the human-powered entry into Troy.
episodes.functionalUnit: Construction, regional supply, one-way human-powered entry into Troy and assumed end-of-life destruction of one full-scale wooden horse capable of concealing and delivering 50 equipped warriors.

evidence.basis: Ancient sources constrain timber origin, hollow form, 50-warrior capacity, wheels, ropes and build logic. Dimensions, timber volumes, fasteners and regional freight are explicit engineering assumptions.
evidence.uncertainty: Rope mass and the reconstructed timber bill of materials materially influence the result; the published rope sensitivity spans 7.0–9.7 t CO₂e.

episodes.title: Excalibur
episodes.hotspot: The charcoal route contributes 52.2 kg CO₂e, or 71.0% of the forty-year result.
episodes.featuredDescription: Arthur's lake-born blade reconstructed as a 1.71 kg late-medieval sword with scabbard over 40 years: the object is light, but bloomery ironmaking and inefficient charcoal production place 517 kg of dry-wood equivalent behind its steel.
episodes.functionalUnit: Provision, use and maintenance of one complete Excalibur sword and scabbard over 40 years of Arthurian rule, including manufacture, one replacement scabbard, blade care and return to the lake.

evidence.basis: Malory provides the narrative constraints; the Royal Armouries supplies a measurable late-medieval sword analogue; bloomery ironmaking is reconstructed from an experimental analogue.
evidence.uncertainty: Charcoal yield controls the upstream wood demand and the process-energy hotspot, making the ironmaking reconstruction the principal sensitivity.

episodes.title: The Tower of Babel
episodes.hotspot: Fired-brick facing contributes 95.4% of the footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: A 90 m ziggurat reconstructed from Etemenanki: most of the masonry is sun-dried earth, yet the fired-brick skin carries almost the entire climate burden.
episodes.functionalUnit: Provision and operation of one completed 90 m Tower of Babel for one year, including full construction, one year of maintenance and auxiliary fires.

evidence.basis: Etemenanki supplies the physical analogue for the completed 90 m ziggurat. Upper tiers, shell thickness, stair volume and material split remain explicit engineering assumptions.
evidence.uncertainty: The fired-brick shell geometry and process intensity dominate the result because fired masonry contributes 95.4% of the footprint.

episodes.title: The Flying Dutchman
episodes.hotspot: Construction represents 97.4% of the one-year footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: A cursed East Indiaman that sails forever without fuel: the operational year is light, while metal armament, fittings and the vessel itself carry the carbon burden.
episodes.functionalUnit: One year of continuous cursed navigation, including full vessel construction, one year of maintenance and auxiliary use.

evidence.basis: Batavia provides the main physical analogue and Vasa a contemporary scale check. The curse belongs to the narrative while vessel geometry and material reconstruction are anchored in historical evidence.
evidence.uncertainty: Charging the full construction burden to the first year strongly affects the headline result; a 25-year allocation sensitivity is therefore material to interpretation.
